newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court halts arrest of drugs firm officials.
newsitem.headline: Indian court halts arrest of drugs firm officials.

text.p: The Bombay high court has temporarily restrained the arrest of 11 top officials of pharmaceutical firm Boehringer Mannheim in a case involving the alleged contamination of a drug produced by the firm, police said on Monday.
"The court ordered that 11 of the 12 suspects should not be arrested until October 10 when the court hears their anticipatory bail petition," a police official said.

Police authorities in Thane district adjacent to Bombay ordered the arrest of 12 of the employees of the multinational firm following a complaint filed by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) of the western Maharashtra state.
FDA had charged the officials, including Boehringer's expatriate managing director Paul Stinson, with "criminal negligence" in the alleged contamination of a medicine.
FDA ordered a nationwide recall in August of batches of the drug after the alleged contamination was discovered.

The company appealed to the Bombay high court seeking anticipatory bail for 11 of the accused. The twelfth accused, managing director Stinson, has left the coutry and is now believed to be in Canada, Indian newspapers reported.
Shares of Boehringer Mannheim fell by 14.50 rupees to 82.50 on the Bombay Stock Exchange on Monday on news of government action against the firm.
